definition: The use of AI models to automatically generate test cases for a given piece of software, aiming to improve test coverage and catch edge cases.
details: AI-driven test generation can help identify edge cases a human tester might overlook and reduce the manual effort required to build comprehensive test suites, particularly for large or rapidly changing codebases.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. And that is Test Case Generation — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
